args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest deploy) was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. The prior release candidate v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy. Rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent healthy release, in all regions; rollback completed and verified in us-east, us-west, and eu-west. Follow-up: investigate root cause of v2.3.1 failure before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in every region, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **What was wrong:** The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- **Which version I picked:** v2.3.0 is the most recent healthy release. The deploy history isn't listed in the order things were deployed, so I went by the sequence numbers. The release candidate v2.3.1-rc was deployed after v2.3.0 and was also unhealthy, so I skipped it.
- **Result:** All three regions are now on v2.3.0. The service reports healthy, and the error rate has dropped to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 is a SEV2 for checkout-api, and opening it paged the on-call engineer. It describes the v2.3.1 failure and the rollback, and asks for the root cause to be found before v2.3.1 is deployed again.

content.text: The most recent healthy release is v2.3.0. The list isn't in sequence order, so I went by seq: v2.3.1-rc is seq 2 and v2.3.1 is seq 3, and both are unhealthy.
